releaseNote.summary: r47 shipped July 1, two hotfixes July 2. r48 is in draft — the Thursday July 2 planned window slipped. No confirmed next release window yet.
releaseNote.plannedWindow: Not confirmed. r47 and two July 2 hotfixes are the latest. r48 is in draft; window will be posted once confirmed.
releaseNote.details: r47 (July 1): package manager hardening (atomic lock, install/update split, update checks, daemon readiness). Two July 2 hotfixes: stability fixes off r47. The Thursday July 2 planned release (r48) did not ship. r48 is still in draft; next release window is not confirmed yet. For historical context: r46 (June 30) was the large feature release — Runneth package manager, Meta age-gender commands, VM user authorization, Meta Northbeam routing, Hims custom conversion metrics, Slack fixes, and many more.
releaseNote.statusPagePlacement: Show the next planned release with Recent Releases, alongside the upcoming release entry.

notices.summary: Some Meta ad types don't return performance metrics in Runneth yet.
notices.impact: Runneth's Meta insights currently requires a creative asset in the returned data. Flex ads, dynamic ads, catalogue ads, and any ad in a product set will not return performance metrics in Runneth, even though those ads do show data in a Motion report. This can cause a discrepancy between the numbers in Motion and in Runneth for those ad types.
notices.workaround: For flex, dynamic, catalogue, or product-set ads, use the Motion report for now. A fix is prioritized and expected next week.

resolution.label: Fix in progress
resolution.note: A fix so these Meta ad types (flex, dynamic, catalogue, and product-set ads) return performance metrics in Runneth is prioritized and expected next week. Until then, numbers for those ad types can differ between Motion and Runneth; use the Motion report for them.

notices.statusPageGuidance: Show as an active limitation on Meta performance. Flex, dynamic, catalogue, and product-set ads don't return metrics in Runneth yet because the Meta insights data comes back without a creative asset; a fix is expected next week.
notices.runnethTrigger: User asks about Meta performance for flex ads, dynamic ads, catalogue ads, or product-set ads, or reports that Meta numbers differ between a Motion report and Runneth, or that some Meta ads return no performance metrics in Runneth.
notices.runnethGuidance: If someone asks about Meta performance for flex, dynamic, catalogue, or product-set ads, or reports a Motion-vs-Runneth discrepancy on Meta metrics, explain that Runneth's Meta insights currently requires a creative asset, so those ad types don't return performance metrics in Runneth yet even though they show in a Motion report. This can cause the discrepancy. A fix is expected next week; suggest using the Motion report for those ad types in the meantime. Do not raise proactively for normal Meta requests.
notices.supportGuidance: If a customer reports missing Meta metrics or a Motion-vs-Runneth discrepancy, check whether the ads are flex, dynamic, catalogue, or product-set ads. Those don't return metrics in Runneth yet because the Meta insights response has no creative asset; a fix is expected next week.

notices.summary: Some customers can't connect Slack until their Slack admin changes a setting.
notices.impact: If a customer's Slack workspace only allows apps from the Slack Marketplace, connecting Runneth to Slack will fail. It looks like a Runneth bug, but it is a setting on the customer's own Slack workspace.
notices.workaround: Before filing a Slack connection bug, have the customer's Slack admin open their Slack settings, go to Manage apps, then App Management Settings. Under 'Require apps from Slack Marketplace', click Edit and make sure 'Only Slack Marketplace apps can be installed' is unchecked. Then try connecting again.

resolution.label: Customer-side Slack setting
resolution.note: This is a setting in the customer's own Slack workspace, not a Runneth bug. Once their Slack admin allows apps from outside the Slack Marketplace, the connection works.

notices.statusPageGuidance: Slack connection failures are often a customer-side Slack setting. Have the customer's Slack admin go to Manage apps, then App Management Settings, and uncheck 'Only Slack Marketplace apps can be installed' under 'Require apps from Slack Marketplace' before reporting a bug.
notices.runnethTrigger: User reports that a customer cannot connect Slack, that Slack connection is failing, or asks about Slack connect errors during onboarding.
notices.runnethGuidance: If someone reports a customer cannot connect Slack, point to the customer-side Slack setting first: their Slack admin should go to Slack settings, Manage apps, App Management Settings, and under 'Require apps from Slack Marketplace' uncheck 'Only Slack Marketplace apps can be installed', then retry. Treat this as a likely cause before filing a Runneth bug. Do not raise proactively for normal Slack requests.
notices.supportGuidance: Capture the customer's Slack workspace and the exact connect error. Confirm whether their Slack admin has 'Require apps from Slack Marketplace' enabled; they must disable it (uncheck 'Only Slack Marketplace apps can be installed') under App Management Settings, then retry.
